patch_description: Replace the slow softmax-Powell multi-start with a fast, deterministic direct-coordinate local search using gradient-informed moves: identify the worst triangle and move its three vertices perpendicular to their opposite sides (the exact gradient directions of that triangle's area), projecting back onto the triangle for feasibility. A shrinking step anneals the search, and randomized escape moves on the worst triplet avoid local stalls. This is far cheaper per iteration than the smooth-softmin Powell approach (which pays softmax+exp+log over 165 triples per function call), so many restarts fit well under the previous 15.8s runtime while improving the achievable min area.
